findings: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp: the only code change widens the SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter gate from SEMI to SEMI or ANTI. The other guards stay the same: one DelimGet, one INNER/SEMI join with only colref = colref conditions, and a SubqueryIsSimple RHS. This covers a natural class of queries, correlated NOT EXISTS on plain equality. Nothing in it refers to a particular query, table or literal.

Removing the join with the DelimGet is already correct for ANTI; it is the same rewrite the upstream code applies when the LHS has no selection. The change only stops the selection from forcing that join to stay.

NULL handling after the NDF-to-= conversion holds. The RHS column is non-null because RemoveJoinWithDelimGet adds IS NOT NULL, so for a NULL LHS key NDF gives FALSE and = gives NULL. Both mean no match, so ANTI still emits the row. Plain ANTI: the LHS is the probe side, and a NULL probe key emits the row as unmatched. RIGHT_ANTI: the LHS is the build side, and PropagatesBuildSide(RIGHT_ANTI) is true (join_type.cpp:14), so NULL build keys stay in the hash table and are emitted by the unmatched scan.

Join filter pushdown stays sound. GenerateJoinFilters still skips plain ANTI (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:238), so the probe-side LHS is never filtered. Only RIGHT_ANTI, which emits build-side rows only, gets probe-side min/max and BF filters.
The diff does not touch timing, settings, tests or anything outside the optimizer, and the two comment edits match the new behaviour.
